text:
Alex (Marketing): Quick: we need a fresh, field-ready battlecard + routing rules for the webinar launch and the follow-up benchmark post. Deliverables: 1-page AE card, 2-line SDR hooks (startup/enterprise), and HubSpot routing map.
Pri (Product): Agree. Focus on three crisp claims: stable p95 under load, identical API across hosted/dedicated/private, and built-in cost controls (batching + prefix caching). I'll attach microbench numbers for ModelZ by EOD.
Zoe (Sales): SDR hooks (rough):
- Startup: "Curious how your inference cost changes as users grow?"
- Enterprise: "We help ops teams avoid surprise bills and rollout headaches."
I'll compress to 2 lines each.
Ben (Growth): Routing pseudo-rule (HubSpot):
```
if (form.expected_monthly_tokens >= 1e9 || company.employees >= 800) route = 'enterprise-demo';
else if (form.role contains 'engineer' && form.use_case == 'prototype') route = 'webinar-or-tech-demo';
else route = 'nurture-marketing';
```
We should add a hidden est_tokens field and an opt-in checkbox for private deployment interest.
AE-bot: Webinar infra check: Friday 09:00 PDT reserved. Deploy status: green. Assets: https://drive.redwood/webinar/launch-2025 (public).
Alex (Marketing): Competitive angle to test vs cloud APIs: "Cloud APIs simplify model access; Redwood simplifies serving for when customers go live." Need this on the battlecard as a one-liner.
Pri (Product): Microbench plan: compare ModelZ on CloudAPI_Y (managed), Self-host baseline, Redwood-hosted, and Redwood-Dedicated. Metrics: cold-start p95, sustained p95 at 800 concurrent sessions, and tokens_per_usd. I will note caveats: sequence length, batch policy, and quantization.
Zoe (Sales): AE one-liners for slide: "Predictable serving, not surprise bills" or "Ship features, not ops runbooks." Which lands? Thoughts?
Ben (Growth): CTA A/B test: "Join webinar" vs "See cost demo". High token est should auto-escalate to AE with a calendar link in the confirmation email.
Alex (Marketing): Owners: Pri -> bench + battlecard; Zoe -> SDR cheats + AE one-liners; Ben -> HubSpot routing + CTA tests; Alex -> slides & webinar copy. Drafts by Tuesday noon.
Pri (Product): I'll include CSVs and a tiny methodology note. Also add a short line about quantization quality tradeoffs.
Zoe (Sales): I'll draft procurement bullets: pricing options (on-demand + reserved), SLA summary, and data residency. Keep each to 2 lines.
Ben (Growth): I'll add the routing mapping to the shared doc and wire the hidden field. We'll test in staging.
Alex (Marketing): Final note for webinar narrative: 8m market context, 12m latency/cost demo (real customer example + chart), 20m live demo showing fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated -> lite-quant), 10m Q&A. Slide headline: "When serving is the product."
Zoe (Sales): Adding quick rebuttals vs self-host and vs managed cloud: ops overhead, kernel tuning, and rollout risk. Short bullets incoming.
Alex (Marketing): Thanks all. Post drafts here when ready and tag me. :rocket:
